plain_english_policy: This bill proposes a constitutional amendment to establish an Alabama Lottery. The policy direction is to create a state-run lottery corporation that operates games of chance, with the explicit prohibition on operating casinos within the state. All net proceeds from this new lottery are dedicated exclusively to two specific educational purposes: funding scholarships for A/B Honor Roll students and providing $50 million annually to help local public school systems hire resource officers. The bill includes a safeguard ensuring these new funds do not replace or supplant existing education revenues.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would permanently alter the state constitution by legalizing lotteries for educational funding while simultaneously banning casinos, creating a dedicated revenue stream (the Lottery Trust Fund) that supplements rather than replaces current school budgets to fund scholarships and resource officer salaries.
sponsorship_supports_position: The sponsors affirmatively advanced the bill as written.
evidence_quotes: "to establish an Alabama Lottery to fund certain Education Trust Fund programs... and to prohibit the operation of casinos in the State."

"Funds deposited into the Education Trust Fund which are derived from the Alabama Lottery shall not replace or supplant existing or any other funds dedicated or intended for the purposes of such Fund."

"Monies in the Lottery Trust Fund shall be allocated and disbursed to the Education Trust Fund to be used exclusively (a) to provide $50 million annually...; and (b) the remainder to provide scholarships"
